In transformer models, the KV cache stores intermediate attention keys and values for previously generated tokens to avoid redundant computation during autoregressive generation. A prefix cache allows the system to share these cached states across multiple requests that begin with an identical sequence of tokens (the "prefix"). However, since GPU memory is finite, the system must decide which prefixes to keep in the cache and which to evict when space runs out. Eviction policies determine the order and criteria for removing less useful prefix entries to make room for new, high-value contexts.

The core mechanism behind prefix-cache eviction revolves around the reuse potential of a given prefix. When a new request arrives, the system attempts to match its initial tokens against existing entries in the KV cache. If a match is found, the system can skip re-computing attention for those tokens, significantly reducing latency and increasing throughput.
